ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-matching action head for multi-domain in-context control
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer on offline trajectories from eight continuous-control domains, including robot manipulation, locomotion, humanoid control and building energy management. Replace the usual softmax output with a conditional flow-matching head that reads the query state and the in-context transitions, then integrates a learned vector field for ten steps to emit an action. Train on two million context-query pairs and hold out forty tasks across the domains. Evaluate normalized return after five episodes in which the agent fills its own context with its own transitions.
CONTROLS: Compare against a single Gaussian head and a mixture density head on the same backbone and data. Compare against a multi-task behavior cloning transformer that never reads context. Run three independent training runs per variant and report the spread of returns.
COST: 840
PREDICTION: The flow head should lift normalized return on held-out tasks whose expert data show several action modes. It may fail to help on domains with narrow expert behavior, where the Gaussian head already suffices, and the ten integration steps add sampling time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-agnostic tokenization for transformer agents across control families
PROPOSAL: Design a tokenizer that turns every state vector and action vector into a fixed number of learned tokens, whatever the dimensionality of the environment. Give each domain a small linear encoder and decoder pair, zero-fill short vectors to a common width of 128 and attach a learned domain embedding. Pretrain the Decision Pretrained Transformer on trajectories from eight domains, including autonomous driving, industrial process control and partial differential equation control. Test on tasks from two further domains that never appear in pretraining, using five expert demonstrations as context.
CONTROLS: Compare the per-domain encoders with one shared encoder fed truncated vectors, and with encoders whose weights stay frozen at initialization. Compare token counts of 4, 8 and 16 per state. Report returns on the two unseen domains over four independent runs.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Per-domain encoders should transfer to the unseen domains better than the shared encoder, because dimensionality information survives. When frozen encoders do as well as learned ones, the gain comes from the backbone and the tokenizer idea is refuted.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How many pretraining domains does in-context control need
PROPOSAL: Pretrain four versions of one transformer on two, four, six and eight domains, keeping the total number of trajectories constant at three million so that data volume does not drive the comparison. Draw the domains from robot locomotion, manipulation, HVAC control, driving and industrial process control in a fixed order. Use a conditional flow-matching action head throughout. Evaluate every version on the same 30 tasks from domains absent from all four corpora, with the agent filling its context from its own interaction over six episodes, and plot normalized return against the number of pretraining domains.
CONTROLS: Compare each version with a model trained on the full three million trajectories from a single domain. Compare against a version trained on eight domains but with task identity shuffled across trajectories. Use three independent runs per version.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Return on unseen domains should rise with the number of pretraining domains and then flatten. A flat curve from the start would mean diversity does not matter at this scale, and a drop at eight domains would point to capacity limits in the backbone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration-prompted adaptation to unseen continuous-control tasks
PROPOSAL: Prompt the pretrained agent with expert demonstrations on 30 unseen tasks and score the first attempt, with demonstration counts of one, three, five and ten. Use tasks from building energy management, humanoid control and partial differential equation control. Build the corpus from expert and learner trajectories, and train a 12-layer transformer with a conditional flow-matching head on it. Add a second prompt type in which half of the demonstrations come from a weaker policy, to measure how quickly returns degrade with demonstration quality. Record normalized return against the number of demonstrations and the expert return of each task.
CONTROLS: Compare against an Algorithm Distillation model trained on the same corpus, and against a behavior cloning transformer with retrieval over the same demonstrations. Compare against the agent prompted with an empty context. Report the spread over three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Return should climb with demonstration count and approach expert return by ten demonstrations on most tasks. The mixed-quality prompt should cost return, and a result where retrieval cloning reaches the same return would show that the in-context mechanism adds little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness to parametric variations of known environments
PROPOSAL: For each of eight domains, create twelve variants by scaling masses, friction coefficients, actuator gains and link lengths by factors between 0.5 and 2. Pretrain the agent on the original environments plus half of the variants, and keep the other half for testing. Let the agent start each test variant with an empty context and adapt through its own interaction over ten episodes, recording the normalized return after each episode. Fit a curve of final return against the distance between the test variant and the nearest training variant in parameter space.
CONTROLS: Compare against a multi-task transformer that sees no context at all. Compare against the same agent with its context emptied before every episode. Compare variants inside the training range with variants outside it. Report three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 620
PREDICTION: Final return should decline slowly with distance from the training variants, and the agent should recover most of the loss within ten episodes. A steep decline with no recovery across episodes would show that adaptation does not reach beyond the training range.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking posterior sampling on a synthetic continuous bandit family
PROPOSAL: Construct a family of one-step continuous tasks in which the reward is a mixture of two Gaussian bumps whose centers each task draws from a known prior. Pretrain the flow-matching transformer on contexts from this family, then compare its sampled actions with the exact posterior over the optimal action, which a closed-form calculation provides at every context length. Measure the Wasserstein distance between the two distributions as the context grows from zero to thirty-two transitions. Repeat the measurement for a Gaussian head and a mixture density head, so that the comparison shows which head family preserves the posterior best.
CONTROLS: Compare the sampled-action distribution with the prior alone at zero context length. Compare against a head trained on the same contexts to regress the posterior mean. Use five independent pretraining runs and report the spread of distances at each context length.
COST: 35
PREDICTION: The distance should shrink as context grows, and the flow head should track the exact posterior more closely than the Gaussian head when the two bumps lie far apart. A distance that stalls after four transitions points to a head that ignores context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context length and ordering in in-context reinforcement learning
PROPOSAL: Train transformers with context windows of 128, 512 and 2048 transitions on the same multi-domain corpus, then test how ordering inside the context affects adaptation. Present the same transitions sorted by time, sorted by reward, and in a scrambled order, and compare normalized return on 36 unseen tasks. Use per-domain linear encoders and a conditional flow-matching head in every run. Collect context from the agent's own interaction for eight episodes, and also from a bank of expert demonstrations, so that both adaptation modes receive the same treatment.
CONTROLS: Compare each context window against a model with a window of 16 transitions. Compare the three orderings on identical transitions. Compare self-collected context against demonstration context at equal length. Use three independent training runs per window.
COST: 2750
PREDICTION: Longer windows should raise return on tasks needing many episodes of exploration, and time order should help most for self-collected context. If the scrambled order scores the same as the sorted order, the model treats context as an unordered set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online self-correction from interaction history on unseen tasks
PROPOSAL: Start each held-out task with an empty context and let the pretrained agent act for fifteen episodes, appending every transition and its reward to the context after each step. Track normalized return per episode on 40 unseen tasks drawn from locomotion, manipulation and driving domains. Use a conditional flow-matching head so that each action is a fresh posterior sample, which makes early episodes exploratory. Report the episode at which the agent first reaches 80 percent of the expert return, and the share of tasks where it never does.
CONTROLS: Compare against a deterministic variant that takes the mode of the action distribution. Compare against a reward-blind variant whose context holds states and actions only. Compare against a multi-task cloning transformer evaluated without context. Use four independent training runs.
COST: 410
PREDICTION: Return should rise across episodes, with the sampling agent exploring more early and overtaking the deterministic variant by the middle episodes. A reward-blind variant that adapts as fast would show that rewards add nothing as a correction signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparison with Algorithm Distillation on a shared multi-domain corpus
PROPOSAL: Assemble one corpus of learning-history trajectories and expert trajectories from ten control domains, and train two transformers on it with the same parameter count and token budget per epoch. The first model follows Algorithm Distillation and predicts the next action from the full learning history. The second predicts the optimal action from a query state and a context of transitions, and carries a conditional flow-matching head. Evaluate both on 30 unseen tasks and on 30 parametric variants of training tasks, once with an empty starting context and once with eight expert demonstrations.
CONTROLS: Give both models identical data, parameter counts and training length. Add a third model that predicts actions without any context. Compare each model on tasks of the same domains, and report three independent runs per model.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The optimal-action model should adapt faster on unseen tasks, while the history model may hold up better on variants of training tasks. Equal returns for both on unseen tasks would show that the training objective matters less than the corpus.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward signal as correction input during in-context control
PROPOSAL: Append the observed reward and the remaining return estimate to every context transition, and compare against a version that leaves both out. Pretrain both versions on the same offline data from eight domains, then change the reward scale and the actuator gains midway through test episodes on 24 unseen tasks. Measure how many steps the agent needs to restore its pre-change return. Use a flow-matching head so that actions remain samples from a posterior that updates with the new rewards, and log the entropy of sampled actions around the change.
CONTROLS: Compare the reward-aware agent against a reward-blind agent on the same perturbations. Compare perturbations of reward scale with perturbations of actuator gain. Compare against a multi-task cloning transformer. Run four independent pretraining runs.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: The reward-aware agent should recover within a few dozen steps after the change, with action entropy rising briefly and then falling. A reward-blind agent that recovers equally fast would mean the dynamics carry the correction, and the reward channel adds less than expected.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-matching action posterior for a multi-domain in-context transformer
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer on offline trajectories from 8 continuous-control domains, spanning robot manipulation, locomotion, humanoid control and building energy management. Replace the discrete output layer with a conditional flow-matching head that reads the query state and the in-context transitions and emits one action by integrating a learned vector field for 10 steps. Each sample is then a draw from the modeled posterior over optimal actions. Use a 12-layer causal transformer with per-domain linear encoders mapping states and actions to a shared width of 512. Train on 2 million context-query pairs and evaluate normalized return on 40 held-out tasks after 5 episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: Pit the flow head against a single Gaussian head and a mixture density head trained on the same backbone, data and training length. Compare sampled actions with expert actions on query states whose logged behavior shows several separate modes. Compare the flow head with a version that ignores the in-context transitions, on those same query states. Average each variant over three independent training runs.
COST: 960
PREDICTION: The flow head should reach higher normalized return than the Gaussian head on held-out tasks with multi-modal expert behavior, and perform alike with the mixture density head elsewhere. It breaks down when the samples collapse onto one mode or when 10 integration steps give worse returns than a single step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-matching action head within a multi-domain in-context transformer
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer on logged trajectories from 8 continuous-control families, among them autonomous driving, industrial process control, partial differential equation control and heating and cooling. Replace the discrete output layer with a conditional flow-matching head that takes the query state together with the transitions in context and produces an action by integrating a velocity field for 10 steps. Every sample then acts as a draw from the posterior over optimal actions the model has learned. Use a 12-layer causal transformer with family-specific linear encoders that feed a shared width of 512, train on 2 million context-query pairs and evaluate normalized return on 40 held-out tasks after 5 episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: Pit the flow head against a return-conditioned cloning model and a retrieval-prompted policy trained on the same data, backbone width and training length. Compare sampled actions with expert actions on query states whose logged behavior shows one dominant mode. Compare the flow head with a version that drops the family-specific encoders, on those same query states. Average each variant over three independent training runs.
COST: 960
PREDICTION: The flow head should reach higher normalized return than the cloning model on the held-out tasks, and keep pace with the retrieval-prompted policy elsewhere. It breaks down once the samples collapse onto one mode or once 10 integration steps give worse returns than a single step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-collected context as the adaptation signal in a multi-domain agent
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer with a conditional flow-matching action head on offline trajectories from 8 continuous-control domains. At test time, start each unseen task with an empty context and let the agent act for 12 episodes, appending every transition together with its reward. Read adaptation as the gain in normalized return from the first episode to the last. Draw 36 unseen tasks from the domains and evaluate each with 5 independent rollouts. Use an 8-layer causal transformer and 1.5 million context-query pairs for pretraining, with per-domain encoders for states and actions.
CONTROLS: Compare the agent with the same weights run on an emptied context. Vary the number of self-collected episodes in context from 0 up to 12. Compare self-collected context with context built from uniformly sampled actions on the same tasks. Report returns on unseen tasks only, with a spread over independent rollouts.
COST: 540
PREDICTION: Return should rise over the 12 episodes and stay above the emptied-context run on most unseen tasks. A flat curve across episodes, or a gain on one domain only, marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-aware context handling in a multi-domain in-context agent
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer with a conditional flow-matching action head on offline trajectories from 8 continuous-control domains, from humanoid control to building energy management. Begin every unseen task with an empty context and let the policy run 12 episodes, adding each transition with its reward. Measure adaptation as the change in normalized return between the opening episode and the closing one. Sample 36 unseen tasks across the domains and give each 5 independent rollouts. Use an 8-layer causal transformer trained on 1.5 million context-query pairs, with domain-specific input layers for states and actions.
CONTROLS: Compare the agent with the same architecture trained with a smaller weight decay. Vary the number of attention heads in each layer from 4 up to 16. Compare the flow head with the same head using more integration steps on the same tasks. Report returns on unseen tasks only, with a spread over independent rollouts.
COST: 540
PREDICTION: Return should rise over the 12 episodes and stay above the weight-decay variant on most unseen tasks. A flat curve across episodes, or a gain on a single domain, marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Parametric variation tests for a pretrained in-context control agent
PROPOSAL: Build 10 variants of each of 6 known environments by rescaling link masses, friction coefficients and actuator gains, with half of the variants lying outside the range seen in pretraining. Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer on offline data from the original environments only, then run it with an empty context and let it correct itself over 8 episodes. Score normalized return per variant and report how return changes as the rescaling factor moves away from 1. Use a diffusion-style action head with 16 denoising steps and a 10-layer transformer.
CONTROLS: Compare variants outside the pretraining range with variants inside it, on the same environments. Compare the agent with a multi-task cloning transformer trained on the same offline data. Vary the rescaling factor from 0.5 up to 2 while the rest of each task stays the same. Report returns over four independent pretraining runs.
COST: 1900
PREDICTION: Return should fall gradually as the factor leaves the pretraining range, with the agent recovering part of the loss across the 8 episodes. A curve that drops sharply just outside the range, without recovery, marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-shift tests for a pretrained in-context control agent
PROPOSAL: Generate 10 versions of each of 6 familiar tasks by nudging body weights, ground friction and motor strengths by factors close to 1, all lying inside the range seen in pretraining. Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer on offline data from the original tasks only, then start it with an empty context and let it correct itself over 8 episodes. Score normalized return per version and report how return changes across the rollout length. Use a diffusion-style action head with 16 denoising steps and a 10-layer transformer.
CONTROLS: Compare unchanged tasks with versions inside the pretraining range, on the same tasks. Compare the agent with a multi-task cloning transformer trained on the same offline data. Vary the rollout length from 100 up to 400 while the remainder of each task stays the same. Report returns over four independent pretraining runs.
COST: 1900
PREDICTION: Return should stay roughly level as the factor moves around 1, with the agent recovering any small loss across the 8 episodes. A curve that drops sharply for the shifted versions, without recovery, marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the action head preserve posterior sampling? A synthetic test
PROPOSAL: Build a family of 200 continuous bandit tasks in which the optimal action is drawn from a known two-component prior, so the exact posterior given any context is available in closed form. Pretrain a small Decision Pretrained Transformer with a flow-matching head on 400 thousand sampled contexts. Draw 64 actions per query and compare their empirical distribution with the closed-form posterior at context lengths of 1, 4, 16 and 64 transitions. Run the same procedure for each head type and chart the gap against context length.
CONTROLS: Measure the distance between sampled actions and the closed-form posterior at each context length. Compare the flow head with a Gaussian head on the same contexts. Compare against the prior alone as the zero-context reference. Report the distance averaged over 200 tasks.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The distance to the exact posterior should shrink with context length and stay smaller for the flow head than for the Gaussian head. A distance that stalls after 4 transitions marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-signal study of the action head in a synthetic bandit family
PROPOSAL: Build a family of 200 continuous bandit tasks in which the optimal action is drawn from a known two-component prior, with rewards observed after each pull. Pretrain a small Decision Pretrained Transformer with a flow-matching head on 400 thousand sampled contexts. Hold out 5 percent of the contexts and log the objective on them at context lengths of 1, 4, 16 and 64 transitions. Run the same procedure for each head type and chart the objective against context length.
CONTROLS: Measure the denoising loss on held-out contexts at each context length. Compare the flow head with a Gaussian head on the same contexts. Compare against the loss at initialization as the zero-training reference. Report the loss averaged over 200 tasks.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The held-out objective should shrink with context length and stay lower for the flow head than for the Gaussian head. An objective that stalls after 4 transitions marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration-prompted generalization against an existing large action model
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer with a flow-matching head on a corpus of expert and learner trajectories from 8 domains. Prompt it with 1, 5 or 20 expert demonstrations on 30 unseen tasks and score normalized return without any parameter update. Use a 12-layer transformer, 2 million context-query pairs and 10 flow steps. Read generalization as the return gap to the expert on each unseen task, and chart that gap against the number of demonstrations given in the prompt.
CONTROLS: Compare against an Algorithm Distillation model trained on the same corpus and prompted with the same demonstrations. Compare against a multi-task behavior cloning transformer that conditions on the unseen task's first observation only. Compare each prompt length with the empty-prompt run. Report spread over three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 1250
PREDICTION: Return should climb with prompt length and sit closer to expert return than the cloning transformer. Parity with the Algorithm Distillation model on most unseen tasks means the claim of better generalization fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-length study of a pretrained in-context policy on seen tasks
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Pretrained Transformer with a flow-matching head on a corpus of expert and learner trajectories from 8 domains. Feed it 1, 5 or 20 expert demonstrations on 30 tasks drawn from the training set and score normalized return without any parameter update. Use a 12-layer transformer, 2 million context-query pairs and 10 flow steps. Read fit as the return gap to the expert on each task, and chart that gap against the number of demonstrations supplied in the prompt.
CONTROLS: Compare against an Algorithm Distillation model trained on a single domain of the corpus and shown the same demonstrations. Compare against a multi-task behavior cloning transformer that conditions on the training task's first observation only. Compare each prompt length with the empty-prompt run. Report spread over three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 1250
PREDICTION: Return should climb with prompt length and sit closer to expert return than the cloning transformer. Parity with the Algorithm Distillation model on most training tasks means the claim of better fit fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-domain scaling of a Decision Pretrained Transformer
PROPOSAL: Collect offline trajectories from 12 continuous-control domains whose observation and action dimensions differ, then pretrain one transformer on all of them at once. Give each domain its own linear encoder and decoder that map vectors of any length to a shared token width, and add a learned domain embedding. Train on 3 million context-query pairs. Evaluate normalized return on 24 tasks from 4 domains left out of pretraining, with a context of 8 demonstrations per task, and compare each held-out score with the expert return of that domain.
CONTROLS: Compare against single-domain versions of the transformer trained on each domain alone. Compare a version without domain embeddings against the full model. Report returns across three independent runs.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Held-out return should reach a large share of expert return on most of the 4 left-out domains. A result near that of the single-domain versions would mean the shared model gains nothing from diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model scaling of a Decision Pretrained Transformer on legged robots
PROPOSAL: Collect offline trajectories from one family of legged robots with identical observation and action dimensions, then pretrain transformers of growing depth and width on all of it at once. Give every robot the same linear encoder and decoder, and train on 3 million context-query pairs. Evaluate normalized return on 24 terrain tasks from 4 robot variants seen in pretraining, with a context of 8 demonstrations per task, and compare each score with the expert return of that robot.
CONTROLS: Compare larger transformers with smaller ones on the same robots. Compare a version without terrain features against the full model. Report returns across three independent runs.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Return should climb with parameter count and reach a large share of expert return on most of the 4 robot variants. A result near that of the smallest transformer would mean extra parameters add little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native posterior sampling with a flow-matching action head
PROPOSAL: Train a conditional flow-matching head on a shared trunk of a Decision Pretrained Transformer, using offline data from tasks whose experts act in several distinct ways, such as grasping from the left or the right and gaits with different footfall patterns. Draw actions natively by integrating the learned velocity field from Gaussian noise for 8 steps. Measure mode coverage on 20 held-out query states with 128 sampled actions each, and compare the pooled samples with the expert distribution estimated from 50 logged demonstrations per state.
CONTROLS: Compare against a single Gaussian head and a mixture density head on the same trunk. Report mode coverage and distribution distance at each held-out state, over three independent training runs.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The flow head should cover most expert modes at the held-out states, and the Gaussian head should land between them. A flow head that covers one mode only marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenization of past transitions for a Gaussian-output in-context policy
PROPOSAL: Train a Decision Pretrained Transformer with a Gaussian output on offline data from tasks whose experts act in several distinct ways, such as grasping from the left or the right and gaits with different footfall patterns, and study how past transitions enter the context. Encode each transition as one token, as separate tokens for state, action and reward, or as pooled chunks of 8 transitions. Measure return on 20 held-out tasks with 128 rollouts each, and compare the encodings on the same trajectories logged from 50 demonstrations per task.
CONTROLS: Compare against a transformer with learned positional embeddings and one with rotary embeddings on the same trunk. Report return and training stability for each encoding, over three independent training runs.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: One of the encodings should give clearly higher return at the held-out tasks, and the pooled chunks should land between the others. Equal return across encodings marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online correction from interaction history on unseen tasks
PROPOSAL: Run the pretrained agent online on 30 unseen tasks with an empty starting context. After each step, append the transition and its reward to the context, and let the agent act for 10 episodes. Record normalized return per episode and the number of episodes needed to reach 80 percent of the expert return. Pretrain on offline data from 8 continuous-control domains with a flow-matching head, a 10-layer transformer and 2 million context-query pairs.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same agent with its context reset before every episode. Compare against a multi-task cloning transformer that reads no context. Report the spread across 4 independent pretraining runs.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Return should rise over the 10 episodes and the agent should reach 80 percent of expert return on a majority of tasks. A curve that stays level across episodes marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offline action prediction accuracy on logged data from unseen tasks
PROPOSAL: Score the pretrained agent on logged transitions from 30 unseen tasks, using a context of transitions drawn from the same logs. Replay each logged state in turn and compute the error between the predicted action and the logged expert action, over 10 chunks of each log. Record error per chunk and the chunk count needed to reach 80 percent of the best error. Pretrain on offline data from 8 continuous-control domains with a flow-matching head, a 10-layer transformer and 2 million context-query pairs.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same agent with its context emptied before every chunk. Compare against a multi-task cloning transformer that reads no context. Report the spread across 4 independent pretraining runs.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Error should fall over the 10 chunks and the agent should reach 80 percent of the best error on a majority of tasks. An error curve that stays level across chunks marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration prompting on unseen tasks across control domains
PROPOSAL: Prompt the pretrained agent with expert demonstrations on 36 tasks absent from pretraining, spanning driving, industrial process control and partial differential equation control, and score normalized return on the first attempt. Give 1, 4 or 16 demonstrations per task. Pretrain on 2.5 million context-query pairs with a flow-matching head and a 12-layer transformer. Report return against demonstration count and against the expert return on each task.
CONTROLS: Compare against an Algorithm Distillation model prompted with the same demonstrations. Compare against a cloning transformer that retrieves the nearest demonstration. Report three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Return should climb with demonstration count and approach expert return at 16 demonstrations on most tasks. Return that stays level between 4 and 16 demonstrations marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context capacity of a pretrained policy across control domains
PROPOSAL: Count how many expert demonstrations fit in the context window of the pretrained agent for each of 36 tasks from driving, industrial process control and partial differential equation control, then examine how attention is spread over them. Give 1, 4 or 16 demonstrations per task. Pretrain on 2.5 million context-query pairs with a flow-matching head and a 12-layer transformer. Report attention mass against demonstration position and against the token count of each task.
CONTROLS: Compare against an Algorithm Distillation model with the same window length. Compare against a cloning transformer that reads one demonstration only. Report three independent pretraining runs.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Attention mass should concentrate on the demonstrations that match the query state, and the window should hold 16 demonstrations on most tasks. Mass spread evenly over positions marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward signal as real-time correction during in-context control
PROPOSAL: Append each observed reward to its context transition and perturb the actuator gains midway through test episodes on 24 unseen tasks. Measure how many steps the agent needs to restore its pre-change return, and compare with a version whose context omits rewards. Pretrain both versions on the same offline data from 8 domains with a flow-matching head and a 10-layer transformer. Log the entropy of sampled actions around the change.
CONTROLS: Compare the reward-aware agent against a reward-blind agent on identical perturbations. Compare gain perturbations of two directions on the same tasks. Report 4 independent pretraining runs.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The reward-aware agent should restore its return within a few dozen steps, with action entropy rising briefly. A reward-blind agent that recovers as fast marks a miss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Embedding structure of domain tokens in a pretrained control model
PROPOSAL: Extract the learned domain embeddings of the pretrained agent and examine their structure on 24 tasks from 8 domains, using a two-dimensional projection and clustering. Measure how well the clusters align with domain families such as locomotion and manipulation. Pretrain on the same offline data from 8 domains with a flow-matching head and a 10-layer transformer. Log the cosine similarity between the embeddings of each pair of domains.
CONTROLS: Compare the learned embeddings against an untrained set of embeddings on identical tasks. Compare clustering from two algorithms on the same embeddings. Report 4 independent pretraining runs.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The learned embeddings should form clusters that follow domain families, with locomotion domains close together. Clusters that match the untrained embeddings mark a miss.
